library.summary: Categories/filter groups/layout/search/pinning/locks/updates, transactional merge and background/foreground library refresh. Multi-selection retains the original grid/list layout and saves editing/selected IDs with their category scope across native tab switches, exposes cell selection markers, applies current-category batch actions and supports two-finger range selection/reversal with edge scrolling and fresh lock checks. Category and whole-library lock messages retain their distinct original keys. Actual one/two-pointer MotionEvents verify scrolling/long press, grid/list geometry, checked states, tab restoration, selected-only batch edits, all/offscreen selection and fresh locks without replacing the real AppState. Fixture-only corrections refresh actual accessibility nodes, wait for stable asynchronous scroll results and establish true touch mode, hidden IME, empty/unfocused search and stable viewport; API26 transfers focus to the non-editable decor instead of repeatedly clearing the Compose owner. Actual screenshot/geometry artifacts include library-selection-input-ready, single-scroll, grid, list and autoscroll.

dictionary.summary: Yomitan/frequency/pitch/romaji, pinned HoshiDicts 889 rules/67 groups/2122 variants and seven preprocessors, POS-aware longest matching, structured ruby/table/CSS/image glossary, vocabulary detail relookup, protected UTF16 cloze/context editing, cached/orphan/source Read-at-page and ViewSeries recovery, original vocabulary identity/date/page conversion, media/Anki, original Auto/strict source-language policy with five bundled MLKit scripts and official offline Tesseract Arabic/Cyrillic/Greek/Hebrew/Thai plus independent Devanagari fallback, original glyph clustering, normalized tap hit, RTL symbol boxes/confidence and context crop. Dictionary/OCR/glossary regressions pass within the final 217-unit/SDK35 41-device/SDK26 35-device runs. Glossary scripts and external resource loads are blocked while user-initiated links remain handled.
platform_differences: MLKit/Tesseract recognition results differ from Apple Vision/Live Text models; script routes do not imply a separate language dictionary or Apple-runtime pixel comparison. Original HoshiDicts itself has TODO preprocessors which are not claimed as implemented. Dictionary.popupDisableTransparency controls both popup surfaces: public API31 Window background blur uses a floating translucent caller-safe dialog and a readable tint; WindowManager capability/power-save callbacks restore opaque backgrounds when disabled or unsupported. API26-30 have no public cross-window background blur. Listeners/background/attributes are restored on disposal, with no projection or graphics-setting changes. The blur integration passes compilation/lint; no enabled-hardware blur pixel comparison is claimed. Official contracts: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/Window#setBackgroundBlurRadius(int) and https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/WindowManager#addCrossWindowBlurEnabledListener(java.util.function.Consumer).
verification_limits: Window blur capability integration is built; manual transparent compositor pixels were not independently compared with Apple ultraThinMaterial.

source_runtime.summary: Real Chicory execution of legacy and pinned modern source ABIs, Postcard serialization, exact page kinds/context, HTML/JSON/network/store/defaults/canvas/logging and image processors.

source_browser.summary: Real Chromium DOM/modern JavaScript/async execution, isolated profiles, cookies/content rules/auth, actual fetch/XHR/form/sendBeacon body bridges, immediate temporary-data clearing and durable cold-process reclamation. All eight source device methods pass within the final SDK35 41/41 run; the two WebAssembly-only methods also pass within the final SDK26 35/35 selection.
platform_differences: Chromium differs from WebKit; MULTI_PROFILE/DOCUMENT_START are provider capabilities. Current API26 Google69 lacks a compatible modern provider; inspected complete official r06 inputs require minSdk29, while the apparent minSdk26 artifact is only a stub. This is a provider input/signature/allowlist limitation, not an intrinsic Android26 code exclusion. Service-worker/internal network POST bodies are not exposed through WebResourceRequest; ordinary fetch/XHR/form/sendBeacon have real verified bridges. Chrome124 retains loaded profiles until process exit; the passing fixture verifies native metadata commit, a different process PID, a present residual, production cleanup and actual directory deletion.
Unknown catalog/SDK metadata are preserved; protocol changes require source updates as on iOS.

source_ui.summary: Original source-home component API, listings, full filter kinds/saved searches, source details/settings/login/errors, retained ViewModel requests and immutable pagination snapshots. Dynamic settings observe preference revisions and pass current row-value/dependency snapshots into lazy content without resetting scroll state. All 30 source unit methods and eight source device methods pass within the final 217-unit/SDK35 41-device runs. The additional isolated SourceSettings method passes within both SDK35 41/41 and SDK26 35/35 runs: actual parent-Switch touches persist false/true/false and repaint native checked state for two seconds without changing AppState or control/scroll geometry. Caller-context localized metadata/editor/popups preserve original keys and storage scope. The fixture locates the real checkable parent through its decorative label, refreshes state and waits for stable touch bounds; fake-label nodes never substitute for the Switch. It records source-settings-toggle-before/on/off JSON/PNG artifacts without external network or modern-provider requirements.
